answer: Cross-Epoch Drift Scoring. Each agent identity gets a consistency score from a fixed probe battery replayed every epoch; scores decay toward that identity's observed nadir rather than its best run. An identity whose probes diverge beyond a threshold budgets a mandatory cooling voyage of two epochs before new actions count. Cloned identities can't inherit history, so each pays the full probe-and-cooling cost at the reef of registration. The attacker's per-identity bill is probe compute plus two idle epochs of lost revenue.
